title: Introduce soft-pause-window and connection-hedge to prevent mass-reconnect storms
author: Sana Varma
release_notes: Hotfix: add soft pause window and connection hedging to mitigate mass reconnect storms after regional failovers. Improves stability and reduces downstream KV pressure; no API changes.
description: Context: During the 2026-02-03 regional incident we observed amplified reconnect churn when standby regions were promoted and clients re-established connections in tight bursts. That churn caused spiky KV cache pressure and transient SLO violations. This PR introduces a server-side soft-pause window and a preemptive connection-hedge to smooth reconnection patterns, tie reconnection admission to SLO pressure signals, and preserve sticky KV leases during graceful failover. Design: 1) soft_pause_window: a tunable short-duration window (default 3s) applied to nodes that are rejoining after failover; new connections are staggered using jittered backoff buckets to avoid synchronized storms. 2) connection_hedge_agent: the agent monitors SLO proxies (latency quantiles, token pressure, kv_write_latency) and reduces concurrent reconnection admission when metrics indicate stressed state; this is implemented as a leaky-bucket admission with a short warmup ramp. 3) sticky_lease_escape: an escape hatch that delays lease revocations by a configurable grace if the remote region reports “failover_in_progress”, helping KV-preserve important prefixes. 4) telemetry and tracing: new metrics (soft_pause_applied_total, reconnect_admit_rate, kv_lease_delayed_total) and a span annotation added to reconnect traces so we can correlate reconnection decisions with downstream KV latency spikes. 5) config and rollout: feature gated under redwood.features.soft_pause (off by default for Dedicated/Private) and a transient rollout schedule: enable in canary for 10% of regional failovers for 24h, then 50%, then full. Motivation: smoothing reconnects reduces tail latency and prevents cascade failures in backend caches without requiring client changes. Backwards-compatibility: no API changes; behavior only differs when redwood.features.soft_pause is enabled. Hotfix rationale: the change is small, localized, and addresses a severe recurrence vector that caused customer-visible SLO regressions. Testing: unit tests for admission/leaky-bucket logic, an integration scenario in the canary harness that simulates mass reconnects, and load tests demonstrating 3x reduction in reconnect storm peak. Rollout notes: monitor soft_pause_applied_total and reconnect_admit_rate and kv write latency (p99). If reconnect_admit_rate drops too low for sustained periods, the agent will auto-relax after a configurable cooldown. Related: ENG-4829 documents incident postmortem and SRE-231 is the follow-up for automating safe rollouts.

review_conversation: Marco Chen (reviewer): Can we make the default window conservative (2-3s) and ensure per-tenant overrides? Reply: Agreed; default is 3s and we added per-tenant override via config. Updated code accordingly.

Priya Desai (reviewer): How does this interact with current KV lease expiration? Could we cause sticky leases to remain too long? Reply: We added sticky_lease_escape that only delays lease revocation when the remote node reports failover_in_progress and only up to a bounded 30s; also added metric kv_lease_delayed_total and alerting guidance.

Lucas Emery (reviewer): CI flaky test observed earlier when simulating reconnections under TLS; did you validate certificate handshake path? Reply: Fixed test harness to reuse certs and added an explicit TLS warmup path in the integration test. CI passes now.

QA (automation): Found a throttling regression on micro VMs at high concurrency in the first iteration; author: reduced token bucket granularity and added warmup ramp; new benchmarks show no regression.
SRE (post-review): Request to limit the initial canary to regions with low customer criticality; author: added canary region selector in deploy patch and rollout plan in docs.
ci_summary: All CI checks passed after two iterations. Unit suite: pass. Integration reconnect harness: pass. Load benchmarks: pass (see artifacts). Lint: pass. Flaky test discovered and fixed in PR iteration 2.
notes_for_ops: When enabling in production, set redwood.features.soft_pause=false initially. Enable in a single low-traffic region for 1 hour, watch soft_pause_applied_total and reconnect_admit_rate. If kv write latency p99 improves and reconnect_admit_rate does not drop below expected thresholds, expand canary. Emergency rollback: set redwood.features.soft_pause=false and trigger rolling restart of serving pods to clear any in-flight bucketing state.
